FINAL HYPOTHESIS:

Summed social capital (ZCU_AU + Zamber + ZMonument) peaked in the Late Únětice / Old Bronze Age (OBA), with the exact peak value SocCap = +4.238082 achieved in BOTH the centuries anchored at BCE 1400 and BCE 1300 (a 200-yr tied plateau). The chronologically earlier (and therefore canonical first-occurrence) peak century is BCE 1400.

The individual components that rise into the peak are COPPER/GOLD and MONUMENT COUNT. Going from BCE 1500 to BCE 1400: CopperGold jumps from −0.36 to +2.54 Z (+2.90 Z) and MonumentCount jumps from +0.165 to +1.708 Z (+1.543 Z); together they account for essentially the whole +4.58 Z increase into the peak. Compared with the long BCE 3200–1700 (MN/SG/LN) baseline (per-century means CopperGold = −0.39, Amber = −0.14, MonumentCount = +0.26 Z), the peak is +2.93 Z above baseline in CopperGold, +1.45 Z in MonumentCount and only +0.13 Z in Amber. CopperGold is near its all-time record (+2.85 at BCE 1200); MonumentCount is the second-highest in the entire ~3 800-year record (behind +3.95 at BCE 2700, where CopperGold was negligible). Amber is essentially flat at the peak — its own series maximum (+1.54 at BCE 3300) lies elsewhere. The peak therefore reflects a coincidence of very high Copper/Gold trade with very high monument-building during the early Late Bronze Age I horizon, while Amber trade is moderate.

The peak is robust to the choice of time-series method: both the raw per-century anchor values (capital.csv, primary) and the block-mean of the *_inter series in time_series_data.csv (sensitivity) place the maximum at BCE 1400 with the same value 4.238082.

payload.hypothesis: The summed social-capital Z-score peaks in the Late Únětice / Old Bronze Age (OBA), at SocCap = +4.238082, achieved in both BCE 1400 and BCE 1300 (a tied 200-year plateau). The chronologically earlier — and therefore canonical first-occurrence — peak century is BCE 1400. The components that rise into the peak are Copper & Gold (ZCU_AU) and Monument Count (ZMonument): from BCE 1500 to BCE 1400 CopperGold moves from −0.36 to +2.54 Z (+2.90 Z) and MonumentCount moves from +0.165 to +1.708 Z (+1.543 Z), together producing essentially the entire +4.58 Z sum-increase into the peak; both are also far above the long BCE 3200–1700 baseline (CopperGold +2.93 Z, MonumentCount +1.45 Z). Amber (Zamber) increases only marginally into and around the peak (+0.14 Z into it, +0.13 Z vs. baseline) and is not the driver. The peak is a co-occurrence of very high Copper/Gold and very high Monument-Count signals in the OBA horizon, robust to using raw anchor values or block-mean of *_inter (sensitivity peak also BCE 1400 with SocCap = 4.238082)."
payload.workflow: Load data/capital.csv (39 rows, BCE 4300..500 in 100-yr steps; decimal separator is comma) and data/time_series_data.csv (3601 rows, CE −4100..−500). Drop metadata columns (group, color). For each of the 39 century rows compute SocCap = ZCU_AU + Zamber + ZMonument. Locate the maximum (4.238082) and identify ties — both BCE 1400 and BCE 1300 carry identical component values (2.54, −0.01, 1.708082). Adopt BCE 1400 as the chronologically earliest (= largest BCE) canonical occurrence. For each component, compute Δ entering the peak from the immediately preceding century (BCE 1500→1400) and Δ vs. the long MN/SG/LN baseline at BCE 3200..1700 (n=16). Cross-check by grouping time_series_data.csv into 100-yr windows and block-averaging the *_inter series (sensitivity); peak location (BCE 1400) and value (4.238082) are unchanged."
